Reviewed and adding the high-risk items first. (I’ll do a full markup in the doc next.)

High-risk / remove or rewrite:
1) “HIPAA-ready” / “supports PHI”
- We should NOT claim HIPAA compliance out of the box. We can say we support architectures customers use for HIPAA-adjacent workloads, and that we sign BAAs only in specific circumstances (and only once Legal confirms the right product + controls).
Suggested phrasing: “Designed to support regulated and sensitive-data workloads (including PHI-adjacent use cases) with Private/VPC deployment options and strong auditability.”

2) “SOC 2 certified”
- Replace with “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” (or “upon request”). Also ensure we don’t imply customer inherits compliance.
Suggested phrasing: “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; security controls and audit materials available on request.”

3) “Data never leaves your environment”
- This is only accurate for on-prem, and even then we need to define what telemetry/support channels exist. For VPC, traffic stays within the customer’s VPC but control-plane metadata may exist depending on architecture.
Suggested phrasing (Private): “Private deployment options (VPC and on-prem) to meet data residency and network isolation requirements.”

4) “Guaranteed latency”
- Avoid. We can talk in terms of SLO targets / predictable throughput with Dedicated.
Suggested phrasing (Dedicated): “Reserved capacity for predictable throughput and latency targets; SLA options available.”

Approved claim components we can safely use:
- “Private deployment options: VPC and on-prem”
- “Encryption in transit and at rest; customer-managed keys supported (KMS/HSM integrations)” (as long as we keep it “supported” not “required”) 
- “Audit logs + export patterns” (but avoid listing fields unless we confirm current schema)
- “SSO/SAML + RBAC” (avoid “SCIM everywhere” unless we’re sure; we can say “SAML SSO, with provisioning options”)

I’ll send a second note with a consolidated ‘approved language’ block after I finish the markup.

Naomi
—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Alignment • Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Messaging review: Regulated Workloads (landing page + outbound) — claims + approved language

+1 to Naomi’s list.

Two additional guardrails for the landing page and outbound:

1) Avoid “compliant with X” unless we can attach a clear scope + evidence (and usually NDA). Replace with “supports compliance programs” / “built to meet security requirements commonly found in regulated environments.”

2) Avoid implying we’ll “store nothing.” It’s okay to say “configurable retention options” and “data handling controls vary by deployment mode,” but we should point prospects to the Security FAQ / evidence pack request process rather than compressing it into one sentence.

If you want a short line that is both accurate and strong:
- “Deployment flexibility (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) with auditability and customer-controlled security controls for regulated environments.”

Aisha

Here’s a consolidated “approved language” set you can paste into the LP + sequences.

APPROVED (use as-is):

Landing page positioning (headline/subhead options):
A) “LLM inference for regulated workloads.”
   “Run and optimize LLM inference with deployment flexibility (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), auditability, and customer-controlled security controls.”

B) “Deploy LLM inference with the controls regulated teams expect.”
   “Private VPC and on-prem options, audit logs, encryption with customer-managed keys, and role-based access—built for production performance.”

Security capabilities (bullets):
- “Encryption in transit and at rest.”
- “Customer-managed key support (KMS/HSM integrations) for Private deployments.”
- “Audit logs and export patterns to support internal review and investigations.”
- “SSO (SAML) and role-based access controls (RBAC).”
- “Configurable retention options (by deployment mode).”

Compliance / evidence wording:
- “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.”
- “Security documentation and evidence pack available upon request (may require NDA).”

Dedicated vs Private safe phrasing:
- Dedicated: “Reserved capacity for predictable throughput and latency targets; SLA options available.”
- Private: “Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) to meet data residency and network isolation requirements.”

CTA (safe):
- “Request a security review + reference architecture”
- “Talk to Security & Solutions Engineering”

DO NOT SAY (remove from all external-facing copy unless Security explicitly approves for a specific deal):
- “HIPAA-ready,” “HIPAA compliant,” “supports PHI” (use “PHI-adjacent” + “designed to support regulated workloads”)
- “SOC 2 certified” (use “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA”)
- “Guaranteed latency” (use “targets” / “SLA options”)
- “Data never leaves your environment” / “we store nothing”
- “We are compliant with <customer’s specific regulation>” (unless tightly scoped + evidence and Legal aligned)

NDA guidance for SDRs:
- Without NDA: high-level security overview, control summaries (encryption, SSO, audit logs), deployment model descriptions
- Under NDA: SOC 2 Type II report, detailed evidence pack items, pen test summaries, detailed architecture diagrams beyond what’s in public docs

If the LP needs one short “compliance-safe” paragraph, use:
“Redwood Inference supports regulated and sensitive-data workloads with private deployment options, strong auditability, and customer-controlled security controls. Detailed security documentation and audit materials are available upon request and may require NDA.”

Naomi

All — consolidating Naomi + Aisha + Elliot into the final block for use across LP + outbound. Consider this the source of truth for the pilot.

FINAL APPROVED LANGUAGE (Regulated Workloads)

Headline/subhead (recommended):
“LLM inference for regulated workloads.”
“Deploy and optimize LLM inference with deployment flexibility (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), auditability, and customer-controlled security controls.”

Approved security bullets:
- Encryption in transit and at rest
- Customer-managed key support (KMS/HSM integrations) for Private deployments
- Audit logs and export patterns to support internal review and investigations
- SSO (SAML) and RBAC
- Configurable retention options (by deployment mode)

Approved compliance/evidence lines:
- SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA
- Security documentation and evidence pack available upon request (may require NDA)

Product lines:
- Dedicated: Reserved capacity for predictable throughput and latency targets; SLA options available
- Private: Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) to meet data residency and network isolation requirements

CTA:
“Request a security review + reference architecture”

Do not say (external):
- HIPAA-ready / HIPAA compliant / supports PHI
- SOC 2 certified
- Guaranteed latency
- Data never leaves your environment / we store nothing
- Compliant with <specific regulation> (unless specifically approved per deal)

NDA guidance (SDR/AE):
- Without NDA: control summaries + deployment options + Security FAQ
- Under NDA: SOC2 report + evidence pack artifacts

Next steps:
- Ben: you’re clear to use the above in Touch 1/2.
- Camila: we’ll align LP copy to this and use Elliot’s footnote (“capabilities vary by deployment mode… may require NDA”).

Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Soojin

Soojin Lee
Product Marketing • Redwood Inference
